Basemap

Each volume runs from its floor to its ceiling in feet MSL, with a thin bright rim at both. Within a class, pale means a low floor and dark a high one. Labels read ceiling/floor in hundreds, so 100/15 is 10,000 down to 1,500. Heights are exaggerated 6× — read the numbers, not the apparent size — and the ground is flat at sea level, so terrain is not modelled.

The SFO Bravo is capped flat at 10,000 across all 17 of its areas, so its shape is in the floor: tilt over and look underneath to see it step down toward the airport.

Drag the compass to spin, the bar beside it to tilt. Double-click to fly in.

Not for navigation. Verify against current charts and NOTAMs.

Airspace and charts: FAA Aeronautical Information Services. Airports: OurAirports. Built with MapLibre GL. Source on GitHub.
